items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: The transcript mentions Eddie South in the context of Rozelle Claxton's decision to leave Ernie Fields' band for South's band. Ernie Fields (the interviewee) does not describe a direct personal or professional relationship with Eddie South, only referencing him as the leader of the band Claxton join

ctx.x: So I thought and I thought, but then it just kind of worked on me, that they said we're with you; if you stay here, there's one man that spoke up--Rozelle Claxton--that had taken Homer's place, said, Ernie, as long as we can eat, I'm going to be here with you, but if you're going back to Oklahoma, I'm going on and hustling me another job, because I gotta go where the money is.

Now, Eddie South had been begging him to join him, a hundred and fifty dollars a week and lodging, doing nothing but playing the white hotels; he says he told him no, I'm with Ernie Fields band, but if you're all going back to Oklahoma, I'm going to tell him I'll accept it. He said now, if any other dates come on, you make up your mind, I'm with you as long as you're here, I'm not going to let you down, but

when you head back, I'm going on with South.
Anyway, I told the guys I'd see
and I got to make a little contact around and
then I talked it over with Willard. He said I
think you shouldn't go back, Fields, but I know
how you feel and it would be a little weight
off me, but he said we have representatives in
that area and they can do something, but I'll
tell you what, you went over really good down
in Philly and if you know you're going to go
back, he called a man--I don't remember him now,
but he said I think he…
